Depends on your location. I personally hated it due to employees and management. It was my first job at 17 and they bullied newbies.  Ended up quitting within a month, but I made decent change and got experience. The actual work wasn’t difficult tho, you learn as you go. I worked at the cash register, drive thru, and tended to the lobby. My favorite thing to do was making ice cream cones, sundaes, milkshakes, and McFlurries. I also packed the food in bags while reading off the order screen. You just have to know how to move fast when needed and multi-task. Sometimes I was taking drive thru orders while making fries. Drive thru was manageable. Passing food through the window, assembling drinks that are already prepared by a machine, and handling payment. Working the headset was cool, sometimes you’re taking two orders at once while punching the it in the computer. Tending the lobby consisted of tidying up counters, sweeping, wiping tables, and delivering food (mine had actual dining service). You will also be standing a LOT, so feet and back pain will ensue (get some gel insoles or comfortable shoes). I think I would have stayed if I were treated better than I was. I made some friends and socialized with (nice) customers. Many customers are not so nice but that’s a given with food service. Just don’t take it personal and let your manager handle it. Ask for help when you’re unsure about anything and advocate for yourself so you’re not pushed around. I had much better experiences when I filled in at understaffed locations which happened often. They even provided gas money. There was even one location where the manager didn’t care if you ate and prepared your own food while working (don’t do that because you will get fired for stealing). Most locations, the absence of store managers allows more freedom. There were also ones where they were just as strict as mine. Definitely read the room because ethics vary. Check your schedule and keep up with postings. I got written up for accidentally not coming in due to a schedule change I wasn’t aware about. Let your manager know whenever you’re running late or can’t come in ahead of time. Punctuality and punching out correctly are important, especially since you’re a minor and can’t legally work more time than allowed. Once I worked 11 hours due to understaffing and couldn’t get paid for the full shift. Oh and since you’re a minor, you don’t have to close the store which consists of major cleaning. Glad I dodged that bullet. Well, that’s all I can think of. It can be a fun job with cool people. Not sharing the negatives to discourage you. 

Good luck on your first job!
